svg.title: What calls what across the FerroHEALTH family
svg.desc: A clinician uses FerroCHART in a browser. FerroCHART expands value sets against FerroTERM and commits compositions to FerroEHR over the openEHR ITS-REST API, which any other application can call directly. FerroEHR validates coded values against FerroTERM. FerroBRIDGE reads FerroEHR over ITS-REST, calls FerroTERM to look up and translate codes, exchanges resources with HL7 FHIR over its FHIR facade in both directions, and writes typed rows into an OMOP Common Data Model database over SQL. Four planned services, drawn dashed, frame the four servers: FerroCHART obtains its token and launch context from FerroSMART, the SMART on openEHR server, and FerroEHR asks FerroSMART whether each token it is handed may do what it asks; FerroEHR feeds FerroPIX, the Master Patient Index, each EHR it creates; applications send FerroFED, the federation gateway, an ordinary AQL query, and it asks FerroPIX where the record is, then dispatches the query to FerroEHR and to other organisations' openEHR CDRs as federation nodes; and FerroSYS, the control plane, spans everything as the band every server reports to. A frame around the eight marks one FerroHEALTH instance serving one tenant; clinicians, applications, FHIR, OMOP and other organisations sit outside it.

g.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD-10, ICD-11, RxNorm, UCUM · the FHIR terminology API
health, telemetry, event log, notifications, configuration · every server reports to it
A dashed outline is a planned product, and a dashed line a call into one.
